transcript:
Header: 2026-03-28 14:30 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Vela Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Vela CTO), Sara Becker (Vela Data Eng)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/vela-poc | benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/vela | SOC2: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're targeting about 45 minutes for the scoping and then any Qs after. quick intros?
00:12 Marcus Lee (SE): Marcus here, I'll lead the technical bench planning and run the initial scripts.
00:18 Priya Nair: Priya - lead ML at Vela, we're building RAG for internal clinical summarization and multilingual patient notes. main concerns are quality on medical text, and p99 latency for UI.
00:29 Tom Alvarez: Tom, CTO - network and infra owner. we'll need VPC options and audit logs for compliance.
00:36 Sara Becker: Sara - data engineer, I'll own the prompt corpus and integration points.
00:42 Speaker 1 (Ava): great. high-level goal for the POC?
00:48 Priya: prove we can get clinically accurate summaries at scale, support English + Spanish + Portuguese, p99 latency under ~300ms for short queries (<=256 tokens) and throughput around 60 qps during business hours. also cost per 1k tokens should be predictable - if it's crazy, it's hard to productize.
01:10 Ava: got it. so success criteria = quality (F1/ROUGE-ish on golden set), p99 latency < 300ms for 256-tokens, availability 99.9, and integration including audit logs. anything else?
01:22 Tom: compliance - SOC2, KMS for keys, and audit trails. We may need private deployment later.
01:28 Marcus: noted. ok on models: since you asked for open-model shortlist, we recommend a small set to start - Llama 2 70B (fine-tuned / instruction-tuned), Mistral Mixtral 8x / Mixtral 7B? (note: sometimes ML names get messy), Falcon-40B-instruct, and Mistral 7B Instruct for a cheaper variant. also consider Flan-UL2 family for strong instruction performance but it's heavier.
01:55 Priya: can you walk tradeoffs - accuracy vs cost and multilingual coverage?
02:01 Marcus: yeah, rough heuristics: Llama 2 70B and Falcon-40B typically give best raw quality on long context summarization, but cost/latency is higher. Mistral / Mixtral variants are often a sweet spot - good quality per GPU and cheaper. For Spanish/Portuguese specifically, some models have better tokenization or training data; Falcon historically lags a bit on non-English but fine-tuning helps. also quantization (8-bit/4-bit) will reduce memory and cost but may slightly impact generation quality - we can test int8 vs q4_0 offline in bench runs.
02:35 Priya: how do you recommend measuring clinical accuracy?
02:38 Marcus: we propose a golden set - 500 labeled examples, include edge-cases and hallucination checks. Metrics: ROUGE / BERTScore + human clinician spot checks for hallucination. We'll instrument hallucination detector heuristics (source overlap, contradicts knowledge base). We'll also collect latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
03:02 Sara: we can provide 10k sample prompts but 500 labeled is doable if we prioritize. we'll try to get that by Monday.
03:09 Tom: about infra - if we run on Redwood Dedicated, what's the network setup? can we do VPC peering and private peering?
03:17 Ava: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private control plane variants via Redwood Private for on-prem later. For the pilot we can do VPC peering with secure peering and firewall rules. Marcus: we'll need a small window for peering setup and test endpoints, usually 1-2 hours.
03:33 Priya: benchmarks: we care about short inference latency for UI and batch summarization throughput for nightly jobs - how do you isolate those tests?
03:41 Marcus: we'll run two benchmarks: interactive (single-shot, <=256 tokens, measure p50/p95/p99 and token latency) and batch (multi-doc summarization, >=1k tokens, measure throughput tokens/sec and overall cost). We'll run each model variant under target qps and 2x target to observe degradation. We'll capture memory/KV cache behavior.
04:05 Priya: what's realistic p99 on Dedicated for Llama 2 70B at 256 tokens?
04:09 Marcus: on a well-configured A100/RTX-like pool, p99 can be ~180-300ms depending on batching and prefix cache. smaller models like Mixtral/Mistral 7B can get p99 ~80-140ms. these are estimates and we'll validate in the run.
04:28 Priya: we also have multilingual prompts and code-switching, that can worsen latency/quality, right?
04:33 Marcus: yes code-switching can impact tokenization and latency marginally; quality differs - we'll include language splits in the golden set. Also we can try bilingual fine-tuning or LoRA on top for critical clinical phrases.
04:46 Tom: security question - do you retain KV cache or customer data? we need guarantees for data residency and logs retention.
04:52 Ava: default hosted mode retains minimal logs; for POC we can opt for dedicated with retention controls, and for Private we can give you full control over storage and KMS. SOC2 docs are on the link shared.
05:05 Priya: timeline - we want a POC decision in ~4 weeks. is that doable?
05:09 Ava: yes: 
- week 1: share dataset and bench plan (this week)
- week 2: Redwood runs model bench and shares initial results
- week 3: fine-tune/LoRA test on best candidate + human eval
- week 4: recap and decision point.
05:21 Priya: ok that's tight but ok.
05:24 Marcus: logistic detail - we'll propose model variants and quant profiles: Llama2-70B int8, Falcon-40B q4_0, Mixtral-8x int8, Mistral-7B q4_0. We'll include cost per 1k tokens estimates in the bench sheet.
05:39 Sara: does Redwood provide tools for A/B testing in rollout?
05:43 Ava: yes Redwood Console supports per-route rollouts, canary, and automatic fallback policies - we'll include config examples.
05:51 Priya: concern about hallucination - what guardrails exist?
05:55 Marcus: suggestions: RAG with source provenance, conservative decoding params (top_p, temperature tuning), and a secondary verifier model for medical facts. We can instrument regression alerts in Redwood Optimize tied to prompts.
06:10 Tom: any limitations on model licensing for open models?
06:13 Ava: we help navigate licenses; some open weights have usage restrictions but for POC we stick to verified open models on the Redwood catalog and will document license terms.
06:23 Priya: ok final recap of chosen shortlist?
06:26 Marcus: Shortlist for bench: Llama 2 70B, Falcon 40B Instruct, Mixtral/Mistral family (7B and 8x variants), and a Flan-UL2 baseline for instruction quality. We'll run quant variants as noted.
06:40 Priya: success metrics confirmed: clinician-rated accuracy >= baseline (we'll define target after 100-lab run), p99 < 300ms for interactive, throughput to support 60 qps, and cost envelope TBD but show per-1k token estimates.
06:55 Ava: next steps - see action items. I'll send pricing and pilot terms, Marcus will share bench harness. schedule will be the wk of 2026-04-06 for dedicated bench run. any final Qs?
07:07 Tom: none from me. thanks.
07:10 Priya: thanks all, we'll get sample prompts to Sara and Marcus.
07:14 Speaker 1 (Ava): thanks everyone, meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional mislabels (Speaker 1 used for Ava), minor mis-transcriptions around model names (Mixtral sometimes transcribed as "Mix trail") and technical terms (KV cache -> KV cash).
